title: Why Use Inflector from DuckDB?
description: The string-shaping toolkit Rails and ActiveSupport made famous, available as DuckDB scalar and table functions. Convert between every common naming convention, pluralize and singularize English words, and rewrite struct keys or whole result sets in one call — without dropping into Python or a UDF.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: ETL and modeling work where the *names* matter: API responses come back in `camelCase`, your warehouse runs `snake_case`, your dashboards want `Title Case`, and your migration script needs `user_accounts` from `UserAccount`. Inflector handles the mechanical part in SQL.

bulletPoints.label: Normalize column names from external sources
bulletPoints.description: CSV / JSON / API ingest with mixed casing — call `inflect('snake', ...)` once and every column comes back consistent. No per-column rename boilerplate.

bulletPoints.label: Reshape struct columns
bulletPoints.description: `inflect` recurses through `STRUCT` keys, so a `payload` column with camelCase fields becomes snake_case in one pass — useful when storing API responses next to native warehouse data.

bulletPoints.label: Generate Rails-style names
bulletPoints.description: Build table names, class names, and foreign-key columns from each other: `inflector_to_table_case`, `inflector_to_class_case`, `inflector_to_foreign_key`. Handy when emitting DDL or migration code from SQL.

bulletPoints.label: Inflect human-readable text
bulletPoints.description: `inflector_to_plural`, `inflector_to_singular`, `inflector_ordinalize`, `inflector_to_title_case`, `inflector_to_sentence_case` — for labels, headings, and the kind of microcopy generated by reports.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Inflector is a thin DuckDB wrapper over the [`cruet`](https://crates.io/crates/cruet) and [`convert_case`](https://crates.io/crates/convert_case) Rust crates — the same Rails-Inflector heritage exposed as scalar functions plus one polymorphic dispatcher.

bulletPoints.label: Two ways to pick a case
bulletPoints.description: One named function per target case (camel, snake, pascal, kebab, train, screaming-snake, title, sentence, class, table) when the case is known at parse time, plus a polymorphic `inflect` that takes the case as a runtime argument when it isn't.

bulletPoints.label: Polymorphic across shapes
bulletPoints.description: `inflect` accepts a `VARCHAR`, a `STRUCT`, or a query — string in / string out, struct in / struct with renamed keys out, query in / query with renamed columns out. Same function name across all three shapes.

bulletPoints.label: Predicates for routing
bulletPoints.description: A matching `is_*` predicate for each case, useful when normalizing a column whose values arrive in mixed conventions.

bulletPoints.label: Rails / ActiveSupport-style helpers
bulletPoints.description: Foreign-key conversion (`Message` → `message_id`), demodulize (`ActiveRecord::CoreExtensions::String` → `String`), deconstantize (`Net::HTTP` → `Net`), ordinalize (`1` → `1st`), and the inverse — the familiar Inflector toolkit, ported to SQL.

sections.title: Caveats
sections.description: What to know before relying on inflection in a production pipeline.

bulletPoints.label: Pluralization is English-only
bulletPoints.description: Singular/plural rules wrap the [`cruet`](https://crates.io/crates/cruet) Rust crate, which ships English rules and irregular forms (`person`/`people`, `mouse`/`mice`). Non-English text returns wrong output silently — keep a real linguistic library upstream for multilingual data.

bulletPoints.label: Case transforms are mechanical, not semantic
bulletPoints.description: `inflector_to_snake_case('XMLHttpRequest')` yields `xml_http_request` — the underlying tokenizer treats acronyms as runs of capitals. That's right for column-naming work; if you need acronym preservation rules tuned to your domain, do that step in application code first.

bulletPoints.label: Pluralization isn't always reversible
bulletPoints.description: `people` → `person` is fine, but English has true ambiguities (`data` is both singular and plural in modern usage; `species` is unchanged). Don't round-trip a value through plural-then-singular and assume identity.

bulletPoints.label: Single-character tokens are skipped
bulletPoints.description: The case tokenizer ignores 1-character runs; this matters for inputs like `aB` or single-letter prefixes. Two-character minimum on tokens.

useCases.title: Snake-case an entire CSV / JSON ingest
useCases.description: Wrap [`read_csv`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/csv/overview) / [`read_json`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/loading_json) in `inflect('snake', ...)` to rewrite every column header in one call. The fastest path from a `firstName,lastName,emailAddress` CSV to a clean warehouse table.

useCases.title: Reshape struct payloads
useCases.description: API responses stored as `STRUCT` columns — `inflect('snake', payload)` returns the same struct with every key renamed, recursively, leaving values untouched.

useCases.title: Generate Rails-style DDL from a class list
useCases.description: From a column of class names, build table names with `inflector_to_table_case` and foreign keys with `inflector_to_foreign_key` — useful when emitting migration SQL from a model registry.

useCases.title: Format report labels
useCases.description: Pluralize counts, ordinalize positions, title-case headings — the kind of microcopy that otherwise pulls SQL out into application code.
